languages.name: Assamese
languages.scriptNote: Assamese is written in the Bengali script. The Assamese alphabet adds ৰ (ra) and ৱ (wa), which are not the same as the Bengali র and ব. The paper is printed in this script, so write the Assamese forms rather than a Bengali transliteration.
traps: Use ৰ and ৱ where Assamese requires them; substituting Bengali র and ব changes the spelling.
Keep the vowel signs (matras) attached to the consonant; do not write the vowel as a separate letter.
The Assamese and Bengali scripts share most letters but not all vocabulary. Do not treat the paper as a Bengali comprehension test.

languages.name: Bengali
languages.scriptNote: Bengali is written left to right in the Bengali script. The script has independent vowels, consonant letters, vowel signs and conjunct forms. The paper tests standard written Bengali, not transliterated Bengali in Latin letters.
traps: The vowel sign ে is written before the consonant but typed after it; do not reverse the order.
Use conjunct forms where standard Bengali requires them instead of writing each consonant separately.
Distinguish শ, ষ and স in spelling; they are not interchangeable in formal writing.

languages.name: Bodo
languages.scriptNote: The UPSC Bodo paper is written in Devanagari. Bodo has its own vocabulary and grammar; it is not Hindi with a few replaced words. The apostrophe in the language name बर' is part of the standard written form.
traps: Write Bodo, not Hindi. A Devanagari passage can still be the wrong language.
Keep the apostrophe in बर' where the standard spelling uses it.
Do not replace Bodo verb forms with Hindi forms; the sentence structure and agreement are different.

sample.passage: सोलोंथाया मोनफ्रोमबो सुबुंनि जिउनि थाखाय जोबोद गोनां। बेयो जोंनो गियान होयो आरो बुहुमखौ मोजाङै बुजिनो मदद खालामो। सोलोंथायनि गेजेरजों सासे सुबुंआ गावखौनो गावनि आखायाव गसंनो हायो आरो मोजां इयुन दाफुंनो हायो। जोंनि समाजियाव, सोलोंथाया गरिबथाय आरो रोङैथायखौ होखारनायाव गाहाय बिफाव लायो। सोलोंथाय गैयैब्ला, रावबो सुबुं एबा हादरा जौगानायनि लामयाव आवगायनो हाया। सोलोंथाया सुबुंनि आखु आरो सोरखौबो मानगोनां खालामो। आथिखालनि जुगाव, सोलोंथाया खालि बिजाबनि सोलोंथायनोल' नङा, बेयो सुबुंनि जुक्ति आरो साननाय-हनायखौबो जौगाहोयो। मोजां सोलोंथाया सुबुंखौ समाजनि सासे मोजां नागरिक महरै दाफुङो। बेखायनो, मोनफ्रोमबो गथ'आ फरायसालियाव थांनांगौ आरो सोलोंनांगौ। सोलोंथायानो जाफुंसारनाय आरो गोजों जिउनि साबि। बेयो जोंनि बिखायाव सिमां आरो फोथायनाय जगायनानै होयो।
sample.english: Education is extremely important for every person's life. It gives us knowledge and helps us understand the world well. Through education, a person can stand on their own feet and build a bright future. In our society, education plays a major role in removing poverty and ignorance. Without education, no person or country can move forward on the path of progress. Education refines a person's character and makes everyone respectful. In the modern era, education is not just about bookish learning; it also improves a person's logic and thinking. Good education shapes a person as a good citizen of society. Therefore, every child must go to school and learn. Education is the key to success and a bright life. It instills dreams and confidence in our hearts.

questions.q: Why is education considered essential for a person's future?
questions.a: Education is essential because it allows a person to be self-reliant and build a bright and better future.

questions.q: What role does education play in society according to the passage?
questions.a: In society, education plays a vital role in removing poverty and ignorance.

questions.q: How does the passage describe modern education beyond books?
questions.a: Modern education develops a person's logic and thinking abilities, rather than just bookish knowledge.

languages.name: Dogri
languages.scriptNote: Dogri is written in Devanagari for the UPSC paper. It is a distinct language with its own vocabulary and grammar, not a dialect of Hindi. The paper tests standard written Dogri, so do not replace Dogri forms with Hindi forms.
traps: Dogri is not Hindi. A Devanagari passage can still be the wrong language.
Use ड़ and ढ़ correctly; they are separate letters, not decorative variants.
Translate meaning and idiom, not word order. A literal Hindi-style sentence often reads wrong in Dogri.

sample.passage: जंगलां दा साड़े जीवन च बड़ा महत्व ऐ। एह् धरती दे फेफड़े न जेहड़े सां साफ हवा ते आक्सीजन दिंदे न। जदुं असीं रुख लांदे आं तां एह् नमी बरकरार रखदे न ते मिट्टी गी कटने थमां बचांदे न। जंगलां च मते सारे पशु-पंछी रेंदे न जेहड़े साड़े पर्यावरण दे संतुलन गी बनाए रखदे न। अजकल दे समें च जंगलां दी कटाई इक बड़ी समस्या बणी दी ऐ। जेकर असीं जंगलां गी नी बचागं तां साड़ा जीवन बी खतरे च पौई सकदा ऐ। इसलई सानू हर साल नवे रुख लाणे चाहिदे न ते जेहड़े जंगल न उंदी रक्षा करनी चाहिदी ऐ। जड़ी-बूटियां दे रूप च बी जंगल सानू बड़ी सारी दवाइयां दिंदे न।
sample.english: Forests have great importance in our lives. They are the lungs of the earth that provide us with clean air and oxygen. When we plant trees, they maintain moisture and protect the soil from erosion. Many animals and birds live in forests, which maintain the balance of our environment. In today's times, the cutting of forests has become a major problem. If we do not save the forests, then our lives can also fall into danger. Therefore, we should plant new trees every year and the forests that exist must be protected. Forests also provide us with many medicines in the form of medicinal herbs.

questions.q: Why are forests referred to as the 'lungs of the earth' in the passage?
questions.a: They are called the lungs of the earth because they provide us with clean air and oxygen.

questions.q: How do trees contribute to soil conservation according to the text?
questions.a: Trees contribute to soil conservation by maintaining moisture and protecting the soil from erosion.

questions.q: What solution does the author suggest for the problem of deforestation?
questions.a: The author suggests that we should plant new trees every year and protect the existing forests.

languages.name: Gujarati
languages.scriptNote: Gujarati is written left to right in the Gujarati script. It uses independent vowels, consonant letters and vowel signs in the same Brahmic pattern as Devanagari, but the letter shapes are distinct. Write Gujarati, not a Devanagari transliteration.
traps: Use the Gujarati script throughout; do not paste Devanagari letters into a Gujarati answer.
Keep the vowel signs attached to their consonants and do not drop them.
Use Gujarati digits ૦–૯ when the passage uses Gujarati numerals.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.scriptNote: Hindi is written in Devanagari. The paper tests standard written Hindi: comprehension, precis, usage and vocabulary, short essays and translation. Keep the register formal and avoid Hinglish in the answer.
traps: Do not mix Perso-Arabic or Latin script into a Devanagari answer.
Watch matras and conjuncts; a missing matra can change the word.
Use standard Hindi vocabulary rather than English words where a common Hindi equivalent exists.

languages.name: Kannada
languages.scriptNote: Kannada is written left to right in the Kannada script. The script has a large set of consonant letters and vowel signs, and its own digits. Kannada and Telugu look similar to a new reader, so keep the two scripts separate in your notes.
traps: Do not mix Kannada and Telugu letters; they are different scripts even where the shapes are close.
Preserve vowel length and the correct vowel sign.
Use Kannada digits ೦–೯ when the passage uses Kannada numerals.

languages.name: Kashmiri
languages.scriptNote: Kashmiri is written right to left in the Perso-Arabic script. It uses additional letters and diacritics that are not the same as Urdu or Arabic. The UPSC paper is printed in this script, so write Kashmiri forms rather than an Urdu transliteration.
traps: Kashmiri is not Urdu. A Perso-Arabic passage can still be the wrong language.
Keep the text right-to-left; do not paste it into a left-to-right block without setting dir="rtl".
Use the Kashmiri vowel signs and letters, not the Arabic or Urdu defaults.

sample.passage: آب چھُ زِنٛدگی خٲطرٕ اکھ بٔڈی ضروٗرت۔ آبہٕ بَغٲر چھُ نہٕ کانہہ تہِ جاندار زِنٛدٕ روٗزِتھ ہیکان۔ کُلؠ کٹؠ، جانور تہٕ اِنسان، سارنی چھُ آبہٕ پیٚٹھ اِنحصار۔ آب چھُ اَسہِ کھؠن رَننہٕ، صَفٲیی کَرنہٕ تہٕ زمیٖنَن مَنٛز کٲم کَرنہٕ خٲطرٕ لَگان۔ اَسہِ پَزِ آب ضایع کَرنہٕ نِش بَچُن تہٕ اَمِچ حِفاظَت کَرنی۔ واریاہن جاین مَنٛز چھُ آبُک قَحط، یُس اَمی کِنہِ چھُ تِکؠازِ اَسہِ چھُنہٕ اَمِیوک صٔحیح اِستِعمال کَرُن یِوان۔ ییٚلہِ اَسہِ آب بَچاوو، تِلی ہیکو اَسہِ اکھ جان مُستَقبیٖل بَنٲوِتھ۔ آب چھُ قدرتُک اکھ انمول تُحفہٕ یُس اَسہِ زایع کَرُن پَزِ نہٕ۔ پننیٚن دٔریاوَن تہٕ ناگَن پَزِ نہٕ گَنٛدٕ کَرُن۔ گَنٛدٕ آب سٟتؠ چھِ بؠمٲرِ پٲدٕ گَژھان۔ صٲف آب چھُ اَسہِ تَنٛدُرُستی بَخشان۔ اَمِہ کِنہِ پَزِ اَسہِ پرؠتھ کَنہِ سَطحس پیٚٹھ آب بَچاوُن۔
sample.english: Water is a vital necessity for life. Without water, no living being can stay alive. Trees, animals, and humans, all depend on water. Water is used by us for cooking food, cleaning, and for working in the fields. We should avoid wasting water and protect it. In many places, there is a scarcity of water, which is because we do not use it correctly. When we save water, only then can we build a good future. Water is an invaluable gift of nature that we should not waste. We should not pollute our rivers and springs. Dirty water causes diseases. Clean water provides us with health. Therefore, we should save water at every level.
sample.topic: The Importance and Conservation of Water

questions.q: Why is water considered essential for all living beings?
questions.a: Water is essential because no living being—including plants, animals, and humans—can survive without it.

questions.q: What are some of the practical uses of water mentioned in the text?
questions.a: Water is used for cooking food, cleaning purposes, and agricultural work in the fields.

questions.q: What is the consequence of using dirty water according to the passage?
questions.a: According to the passage, using dirty water leads to disease, whereas clean water supports health.

languages.name: Konkani
languages.scriptNote: The UPSC Konkani paper is written in Devanagari. Konkani is a distinct language with its own vocabulary and grammar; Roman-script Konkani is used in some publications but is not the exam script. Write the Devanagari form.
traps: Use Devanagari, not Roman script, for the exam answer.
Do not replace Konkani words with Marathi words merely because the scripts match.
Keep the vowel signs and conjuncts of standard written Konkani.

languages.name: Maithili
languages.scriptNote: Maithili is written in Devanagari for the UPSC paper. Tirhuta is the historical script of the language, but the examination paper uses Devanagari. Maithili has its own grammar and vocabulary; do not treat it as a Hindi variant.
traps: Write Maithili, not Hindi. The shared script does not make the languages interchangeable.
Use the Maithili verb forms and honorifics that the passage uses.
Do not switch to Tirhuta unless the question paper itself is printed in it.

languages.name: Malayalam
languages.scriptNote: Malayalam is written left to right in the Malayalam script. The script uses chillu letters and a large set of conjunct forms. Malayalam and Tamil are separate scripts; do not mix them in the same answer.
traps: Use chillu letters where standard Malayalam requires them.
Do not mix Tamil letters into a Malayalam answer.
Preserve vowel signs and the correct conjunct form.

languages.name: Manipuri
languages.scriptNote: The UPSC Manipuri paper has historically been printed in the Bengali script. Meitei Mayek is also used in Manipur, but check the script printed on the current paper before you practise. This page assumes the Bengali-script paper.
traps: Confirm the script on the current question paper; do not assume Meitei Mayek.
Use Manipuri vocabulary and grammar, not Bengali, even though the script is Bengali.
Keep the vowel signs and conjuncts of standard written Manipuri.

languages.name: Marathi
languages.scriptNote: Marathi is written in Devanagari. It has its own vocabulary and grammatical forms; a Devanagari passage is not automatically Hindi. The paper tests standard written Marathi, including comprehension, precis, usage and translation.
traps: Use Marathi vocabulary and verb forms, not Hindi equivalents.
Use ळ where standard Marathi requires it; it is a distinct letter.
Watch agreement and honorific forms; Marathi uses them differently from Hindi.

languages.name: Nepali
languages.scriptNote: Nepali is written in Devanagari. It shares the script with Hindi but has its own vocabulary, spelling conventions and grammar. The paper tests standard written Nepali, so do not submit a Hindi answer in Devanagari.
traps: Use Nepali spellings and vocabulary, not Hindi.
Watch the verb forms and honorifics used in the passage.
Keep the vowel signs and conjuncts of standard written Nepali.

languages.name: Odia
languages.scriptNote: Odia is written left to right in the Odia script. The letters are rounded and visually distinct from Bengali. The script has its own digits. Write Odia, not a Bengali transliteration.
traps: Do not mix Bengali and Odia letters; they are different scripts.
Distinguish ଡ/ଡ଼ and ଢ/ଢ଼ where the spelling requires it.
Use Odia digits ୦–୯ when the passage uses Odia numerals.

languages.name: Punjabi
languages.scriptNote: The UPSC Punjabi paper is written in Gurmukhi. Shahmukhi is used by Punjabi speakers in Pakistan, but it is not the script of this paper. Write Gurmukhi and use the script's own digits when the passage does.
traps: Use Gurmukhi, not Shahmukhi or a Latin transliteration.
Keep the vowel signs attached to the consonants.
Use Gurmukhi digits ੦–੯ when the passage uses Punjabi numerals.

languages.name: Sanskrit
languages.scriptNote: Sanskrit is written in Devanagari for the UPSC paper. The grammar is more inflected than Hindi: case endings, dual forms, sandhi and compounds carry meaning. Do not substitute modern Hindi constructions for Sanskrit ones.
traps: Use Sanskrit case endings and verb forms, not Hindi equivalents.
Resolve sandhi before you translate; do not treat the surface form as a separate word.
Do not add modern Hindi vocabulary where the passage uses a Sanskrit term.

languages.name: Santali
languages.scriptNote: The UPSC Santali paper is written in Ol Chiki, the script created for Santali in the twentieth century. Ol Chiki is not Bengali, Devanagari or Latin; its letters have their own Unicode block. Use the Ol Chiki characters, not lookalike Latin letters.
traps: Write Ol Chiki, not Bengali, Devanagari or a Latin transliteration.
Use the Ol Chiki digits ᱐–᱙ when the passage uses Santali numerals.
Do not replace Ol Chiki letters with visually similar Latin characters.

sample.passage: ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱱᱟᱹᱲᱤ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱵᱚ ᱨᱮᱱ ᱥᱟᱹᱨᱤ ᱜᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ ᱠᱚ. ᱱᱩᱠᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱵᱚ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱡᱤᱣᱤ ᱦᱚᱭ ᱠᱚ ᱮᱢᱟᱵᱚᱱᱟ. ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱵᱚ ᱡᱚ, ᱵᱟᱦᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱩᱢᱩᱞ ᱵᱚ ᱧᱟᱢᱟ. ᱱᱩᱠᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱵᱚᱣᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱭ-ᱦᱤᱥᱤᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱪᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱲ ᱠᱚ ᱫᱚᱦᱚᱭᱟ. ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱬᱮ ᱠᱚ ᱛᱩᱠᱟᱹ ᱠᱚ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱚᱸᱰᱮ ᱠᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ. ᱡᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱦᱚᱭ-ᱦᱤᱥᱤᱫ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱜᱟᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜ-ᱟ. ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱫᱚ ᱦᱟᱥᱟ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱠᱚ ᱫᱚᱦᱚᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱟᱹᱰᱷᱤ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱠᱚ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱵᱚᱱᱟ. ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱵᱚ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱜᱟᱢ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱰᱷᱮᱨ ᱠᱟᱭᱛᱮ ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱭ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ. ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱵᱮᱜᱚᱨ ᱱᱚᱣᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱹᱨᱛᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱤᱭᱚᱱ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜ-ᱟ. ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱜᱮ ᱟᱵᱚ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱚ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱠᱚᱜ-ᱟ.
sample.english: Trees and plants are our true friends. They give us the life-giving air (oxygen) for breathing. We get fruits, flowers, and shade from trees. They keep our environment clean and cool. Birds build nests in trees and live there. For rainfall and climate, trees are very necessary. Trees keep the soil firm and protect us from floods. Therefore, it is necessary for us to plant more trees for the future. Without trees, life on this earth is not possible. If we save trees, we ourselves will be saved.

questions.q: Why are trees described as our true friends according to the passage?
questions.a: Trees are called our true friends because they provide us with essential oxygen for breathing, as well as fruits, flowers, and shade.

questions.q: How do trees protect the physical environment and wildlife?
questions.a: Trees keep the environment clean and cool, provide nesting places for birds, hold the soil firm to prevent erosion, and protect against floods.

questions.q: What conclusion does the passage draw about the relationship between trees and human survival?
questions.a: The passage concludes that life on Earth is impossible without trees, and that saving trees is equivalent to saving ourselves.

languages.name: Sindhi (Devanagari)
languages.scriptNote: UPSC's 2023 Mains paper list includes Sindhi in Devanagari. Sindhi is also written in Perso-Arabic, but this page follows the Devanagari paper. Check the current notification for the script offered in your cycle.
traps: Confirm whether the current paper is Devanagari or Perso-Arabic before you practise.
Write Sindhi, not Hindi or Urdu; the shared script does not make the languages interchangeable.
Use the Sindhi vocabulary and grammar of the passage, not a Hindi paraphrase.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.scriptNote: Tamil is written left to right in the Tamil script. The script has its own digits and a distinctive set of vowel signs. Tamil and Malayalam are different scripts; do not mix them in the same answer.
traps: Do not mix Malayalam letters into a Tamil answer.
Preserve the difference between short and long vowels.
Use Tamil digits ௦–௯ when the passage uses Tamil numerals.

languages.name: Telugu
languages.scriptNote: Telugu is written left to right in the Telugu script. The script has its own digits and a large set of conjunct forms. Telugu and Kannada look similar to a new reader, so keep the two scripts separate.
traps: Do not mix Kannada and Telugu letters.
Preserve vowel length and the correct vowel sign.
Use Telugu digits ౦–౯ when the passage uses Telugu numerals.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.scriptNote: Urdu is written right to left in the Perso-Arabic script, normally in Nastaliq style. The paper tests standard written Urdu, including comprehension, precis, usage and translation. Keep the text right-to-left and use Urdu spellings.
traps: Keep the text right-to-left; do not paste it into a left-to-right block without setting dir="rtl".
Distinguish ہ/ھ and ی/ے in spelling.
Use Urdu vocabulary and grammar, not a Hindi sentence written in Perso-Arabic.
